name: Introduction and overview — C-5 Galaxy — aircraft record
title: Introduction and overview — C-5 Galaxy
description: Introduction and overview of the C-5 Galaxy: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history. The C-5 Galaxy is a four-engine heavy strategic airlifter built by Lockheed, entering service in 1970 and still the largest aircraft in the U.S. military inventory. Its nose and aft doors open for drive-through loading of outsized cargo. 131 were built; the C-5M Super Galaxy upgrade added new engines and avionics. Baseline facts: Four-engine heavy airlifter; service from 1970; 131 built by Lockheed; largest U.S. military aircraft..
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
